SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #7
====

GRADE: Grade 6
SUBJECT: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. watt (W)
   B. newton (N)
   C. pascal (Pa)
   D. joule (J)

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Light? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Light.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Light.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Light.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Light.

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Slopes as simple machines? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Slopes as simple machines.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Slopes as simple machines.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Slopes as simple machines.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Slopes as simple machines.

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Invertebrates? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Invertebrates.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Invertebrates.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Invertebrates.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Invertebrates.

5. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. A chemical reaction forming ash
   C. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

6. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

7. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water removes heat too quickly
   B. Water always increases oxygen
   C. Petrol fires have no fuel
   D. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

8. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 100 °C
   B. 37 °C
   C. 50 °C
   D. 0 °C

9. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Iron rusting
   B. Milk souring
   C. Paper burning to ash
   D. Ice melting to water

10. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   B. Removing all vegetation
   C. Overgrazing continuously
   D. Burning crop residue every week

11. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Glucose and oxygen
   C. Nitrogen gas only
   D. Only water vapour

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Change of State? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Change of State.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Change of State.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Change of State.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Change of State.

13. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. A mixture of two liquids
   C. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   D. Any substance that conducts electricity

14. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Primary consumers only
   B. Decomposers only
   C. Tertiary consumers
   D. Producers

15. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Composition of Air? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Composition of Air.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Composition of Air.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Composition of Air.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Composition of Air.

16. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Levers as simple machines? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Levers as simple machines.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Levers as simple machines.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Levers as simple machines.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Levers as simple machines.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Levers as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Slopes as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Invertebrates and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Change of State and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Composition of Air and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Light and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

23. In three clear sentences, explain Levers as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

24. In three clear sentences, explain Slopes as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
